solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old US soldier sees little point apprehending old woman

indicators.note: to apprehend is to seize or hold, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: minute means tiny
N is a compass point, north
MA is a mother, informally an old woman

explanation.surface: A veteran American soldier notices something tiny as he arrests an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MA as old woman suits an American clue, where mother is Ma; 'apprehending' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutemen were militia in the American War of Independence, ready to fight at a minute's notice.

clue.text: Seriously wound up one in US resort

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' sends the word for seriously wound upwards, back to front; 'wound' does double duty in the surface

parts.note: with 'wound' this reads as to injure badly: to maim
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone gets very tense in an American holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like 'tense', but 'wound' belongs with 'Seriously' as the verb, and 'up' is the reversal signal in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a Florida city famous for beaches and holidays, so it is a resort.

clue.text: Ducks gunshot fired

indicators.note: the shot is fired, scattering its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Waterfowl scatter when a gun goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so ducks are zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket duck is a score of nothing, and a nought is a zero, so ducks are zeros.

clue.text: Sign for the staff meaning rent has been reduced

parts.note: the tenor of a remark is its gist or meaning

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the word for rent goes

parts.note: a rent is a split, a cleft

explanation.surface: A notice for employees announces that their rent has come down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been reduced' cuts the T from CLEFT. 'staff' looks like employees but is the musical stave.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical stave showing pitch; this one marks the tenor range.

clue.text: Wrongly interpret notes: study's genuine

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale; mis are several of them
to con is to study, so 'study is' gives cons
true means real, genuine

explanation.surface: Someone misreads lecture notes, while a study is declared authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to take something in the wrong sense, to misunderstand it.

clue.text: Pick up new rating

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: Someone is collecting a fresh assessment score.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-officer sailor; AB is an able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab is to seize or arrest someone, the police sense of picking up.

clue.text: Fluff caught in back of the hoover, first of all

indicators.note: the abbreviation for caught sits within the initials
takes the opening letter of every word in the phrase that precedes it

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Lint gets trapped in the rear of a vacuum cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' takes B, O, T, H; 'in' puts C between T and H. 'Fluff' looks like lint but is the verb to bungle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fluff a task is to mess it up, which is what a botch is.

clue.text: Vanilla ice, shrinking by degrees

indicators.note: the shortened ice is placed next to the degrees, after them

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees

indicators.note: the word ice gets smaller, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Vanilla ice cream melts away little by little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrinking' leaves IC from ICE. 'Vanilla Ice' reads as a flavour (or the rapper), but 'Vanilla' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla in the figurative sense means plain, with no extras: basic.

clue.text: Watering more seeds planted in a row

indicators.note: the grain head is set into the row like seeds sown in a bed

parts.note: a tier is one row of a set rising in steps
an ear of wheat is the seed-bearing head

explanation.surface: A gardener irrigates further after sowing a line of seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering' reads as gardening but means eyes watering, more tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that water more are more tearful, the comparative of teary.

clue.text: Freudian concept, as espoused by fellow German philosopher

indicators.note: espoused means embraced, so the two pieces are held inside the others

parts.note: he is a male, a fellow
the id is Freud's term for the instinctive part of the mind
e.g., for example, means 'as' in 'animals such as cats'

explanation.surface: A Freudian idea is adopted by another German thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies GER.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Heidegger was a twentieth-century German thinker, author of Being and Time.

clue.text: Theologian seeing beyond a child of five

indicators.note: the word for seeing goes further on, after the rest

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets
seeing as means since, as

explanation.surface: A religious scholar looks past a quintuplet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Aquinas was the great thirteenth-century Catholic scholar of doctrine.

clue.text: Not quite sufficient grounds for consuming dull, starchy food

indicators.note: eating up, so the shortened word holds the other one
almost all, so the last letter of the word for sufficient grounds goes

parts.note: a basis is the grounds that justify something
mat or matt means not shiny, dull

explanation.surface: Coffee grounds, not quite enough, are taken with some bland starchy fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' leaves BASI; 'consuming' puts MAT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain rice, a carbohydrate staple.

clue.text: For Kaiser Wilhelm I, men bringing fabulous flower

parts.note: ich is German for I, as a German emperor would say it
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Kaiser Wilhelm the First's troops present a legendary bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilhelm I' looks like a regnal number, but the I is the pronoun in German. 'flower' is something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ichor is the fluid flowing in the gods' veins, so a legendary flowing liquid.

clue.text: Fair point!

definitions.meaning: the aim or goal of an undertaking

explanation.surface: Someone concedes an argument: good point!
explanation.definitionFit: Unbiased judgement is called objective, and an aim or target is also an objective.

clue.text: After broadcast, see radio DJ quietly threatened

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered like seed, so the letters are rearranged once scattered

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A disc jockey is endangered after a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio talk but signals a rearrangement; P goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be jeopardised is to be put at risk, endangered.

clue.text: What's the most common feature of selfless relative?

parts.words: the most common feature of selfless
parts.note: the word selfless has four S's, more than any other letter
the 's of 'What's' is the word is, read after the letter

explanation.surface: A riddle about the defining trait of an unselfish family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the question as the answer to it: 'S is' the commonest letter in SELFLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sis is the informal short form of sister, a family member.

clue.text: Six pound fifty in change?

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone holds six pounds fifty in loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Spondulix is old American slang, so the whole clue describes some.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondulix is nineteenth-century slang for money or cash, and loose coins are cash.

clue.text: See red and green lasso flying around ring

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the ring-shaped letter
a lasso flying through the air whirls its letters about

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Colours flash as a lasso whirls round a rodeo ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See red' looks like a colour beside green, but it is the definition. Rearranged, GREEN LASSO goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become furious; losing one's rag is British slang for losing one's temper.

clue.text: Ancient character tipped three times to become king

parts.note: eth is a letter of the Old English alphabet

indicators.note: tipped over, so the word for three times reads back to front

parts.note: treble means three times as much

explanation.surface: An old figure wins a triple bet and is crowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' turns TREBLE to ELBERT. 'to become' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelbert was the name of Anglo-Saxon kings of Kent and Wessex.

clue.text: Producing pants soldiers must wear having just finished washing?

indicators.note: the outer phrase wears the soldiers as clothing round them

parts.note: someone just washed is out of the bath
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone makes underwear that soldiers must put on straight after bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is not underwear but breaths: someone panting is out of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panting, gasping for air, is breathless.

clue.text: Beat time in the end for American singer

parts.note: to tan someone is to thrash them
an age is a long time

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A US vocalist ultimately keeps time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The tanager is a brightly coloured songbird of the Americas.

clue.text: Result of being not prepared to back away?

definitions.text: Result of being not prepared to back away?

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: raw food is unprepared, uncooked

explanation.surface: What happens when neither side will retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict breaks out when neither side will give ground.

clue.text: Print taken from court by policeman on duty — case dismissed

indicators.note: the next piece comes after

parts.note: to woo is to court
DC is a detective constable

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case, are dropped

explanation.surface: Evidence from court is taken by an officer on duty, and the case is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case dismissed' looks legal but removes the outer letters of DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print taken from a carved wooden block.

clue.text: Warning to post-holder sporting odd bonnet

indicators.note: wearing in a showy way, here put on with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to a man holding office who wears a strange hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post-holder' looks like someone with a job, but it is a postal envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope holding mail may bear this printed instruction so the contents are not creased.

clue.text: Message to divulge verbally sometime

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to tell a secret is to divulge it
ex means former, sometime

explanation.surface: A message lets someone reveal something by mouth at some point.
explanation.definitionFit: A telex was a message sent by teleprinter.

clue.text: Irish county taking odd returnees from Sligo jail

indicators.note: they come back, so the picked letters read in reverse
the odd letters, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: An Irish county takes in odd prisoners released back from Sligo jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Laois is an inland Irish county in the province of Leinster.

clue.text: Pitcher: you must stop second home run

indicators.note: plugging a gap, so the pronoun goes inside

parts.note: HR is the baseball abbreviation for home run
ye is old-fashioned you

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher is told to prevent a second home run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitcher' fits the baseball scene but means one who shies, throws.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw, so a shyer is a thrower.

clue.text: Cricketer's support to decline

definitions.note: the possessive stands for 'cricketer is', so the noun phrase defines a fielder, and the fielder is named after the position he occupies

parts.note: a leg supports a table
to slip is to fall away, decline

explanation.surface: A batsman's leg support is weakening.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg slip is a rarely used fielding position in cricket, behind the batsman on the leg side, and the fielder there.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder standing in that position is named after it, so this player is a cricketer.

clue.text: Female head vacating unpopular post?

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, leaves

parts.note: spam is unwanted junk mail posted online

explanation.surface: A woman boss leaves a job no one wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' reads as a job but is a message; 'head' is not the boss but the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pam is a woman's name, short for Pamela.

clue.text: Light blue trousers to wear away

indicators.note: used as a verb, to pocket, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: sky blue, the sky is blue
to etch is to eat away a surface

explanation.surface: Pale blue trousers are being worn thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchy account is light on detail, thin, superficial.

clue.text: Copy of Times — I hesitate to say old Times

parts.note: x is the multiplication sign
er is the sound of hesitation
x is the multiplication sign again

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to mention a copy of an old issue of The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To xerox is to photocopy, after the company's trade name.

clue.text: One pondering wet-rot a tidemark shows having returned

indicators.note: the letters read from right to left
the letters are on display inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the damp marks on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' picks the letters inside 'wet-rot a tidemark', and 'having returned' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who meditates thinks deeply, contemplating.
